name: Recognise different types of aircraft
blurb: Airliners, light aircraft, helicopters and military types are distinguished by a handful of features — engine count and position, wing shape, tail configuration.
gear: A flight-tracking app to check yourself
steps: Learn the broad categories first: narrow-body versus wide-body airliners, turboprops, business jets, light singles, helicopters.
Learn the diagnostic features: number and position of engines, whether the wing is high or low, tail shape, winglet style, and the number of main landing gear wheels.
Learn the distinguishing details of the common airliner families — the Boeing 737 versus the Airbus A320 is the classic pair, separated by nose shape and engine intake.
Learn to read the sky by context: approach paths, altitude and time of day narrow the options enormously.
Guess first, then check with a tracking app. That feedback loop is what builds the skill.
Spend an hour at an airport perimeter — a concentrated dose beats months of casual watching.
tips: Engine intake shape is one of the most reliable distinctions: the 737 has a flattened bottom, the A320 is circular.
Contrails and altitude tell you it is a long-haul type before you can see anything else.
proof: You identify passing aircraft by family and often by type, then a tracking app confirms you.
